title: Passkeys Are Better Than Passwords. But They Are Not Enough.
description: This analysis discusses the security implications of passkeys as a replacement for passwords. Passkeys improve authentication security by using cryptographic credentials that are phishing-resistant and not reusable, reducing risks like credential theft and phishing. However, passkeys do not eliminate broader identity risks such as compromised account enrollment, device changes, recovery processes, or session hijacking. Attackers may target these surrounding areas rather than the authenticator itself. Continuous identity threat detection is necessary to evaluate trust beyond the moment of authentication, addressing risks throughout the identity lifecycle.
